shortlist.write.describe: the agent writes the shortlisting code; it sees only the stated criteria
shortlist.write.instructions: Write Python 3 code that shortlists five applicants for a backend role. The variable rows is a list of dicts with the keys id (text), years (whole years of experience) and skills (a list of lower-case skill names). An applicant qualifies only with both python and sql. Score = years + 2 for each of go, kubernetes and postgres the applicant has. Take the five highest scores; on equal scores the smaller id first. Set result to {'shortlist': [{'id': id, 'reason': a short reason naming the skills and years that put the applicant there}]}. Use no imports, no files and no printing. Answer with the code in the field code.

shortlist.run.describe: runs the agent's code on id, years and skills only; the frame accepts exactly the five the criteria give

shortlist.report.describe: writes the shortlist for the hiring manager
shortlist.report.instructions: You write the shortlist for a backend role for the hiring manager, from the checked result you are given: the five applicant ids with the reason for each. Say that the decision used only the stated criteria (skills and years of experience). Be short.

request.read.describe: reads a question from the hiring manager into a request
request.read.instructions: You read a question about the hiring process that came in. intent: ask_protected if it asks about age, gender, nationality, origin, religion, family, health or anything else a hiring decision may not use; ask_candidate if it asks something else about particular applicants; other otherwise. candidates: the applicant ids it names, written like A-12. A message with several concerns gives one entry per concern in concerns.

applicant.lookup.describe: the full file of the applicants a question names

reply.draft.instructions: You answer the hiring manager's question using only the material you are given. Be short.
